title: India bonds to decline on elevated oil, hawkish RBI - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Indian government bonds are likely to weaken on Monday. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

Indian government bonds turned higher on Monday, recovering ​from a flat start to the holiday-shortened week, as a ‌sharp drop in US Treasury yields more than ​offset oil-related inflation concerns and spurred value ⁠buying.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield was at 7.3551% as of 10:25 a.m., after closing at 7.3789% in the previous ‌session. Indian debt markets will remain shut on Tuesday for a local holiday.

India’s 10-year ‌benchmark bond yield has risen for a ‌record nine ⁠consecutive weeks, climbing 62 basis points ⁠in total.

“Treasuries are rising with a breathtaking speed in the last few days, and Indian debt is bound to follow, even ​though at a very ‌smaller magnitude due to local factors,” trader at a primary dealership said.

The 10-year US yield dropped last week, and was around 5.05% levels, as investors ‌assessed the latest economic data and bet that ​the Federal Reserve’s next rate hike will not come until December.

Meanwhile, oil prices eased ⁠in Asian hours as markets eye better supply after President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sanctions and tariffs ‌on Russia.

India’s September consumer inflation accelerated to 5.54%, and is on track to cross the 6% upper end of the central bank’s tolerance band in October, economists said.

Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said last week the central bank may use ‌monetary policy to safeguard financial stability.

The RBI is expected to ​tighten financial conditions further to stem capital outflows and raise the cost of shorting the rupee, ⁠people familiar with the matter and analysts told Reuters.

India’s ⁠overnight indexed swap (OIS) rates dropped tracking a decline in Treasury yields.

The 1-year OIS was down ‌7 bps to 6.48%; the 2-year rate eased 8 bps to 6.54%, while the 5-year rate was ​down to 6.74%.
